transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-06 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Redwood), Emma Li (Copperhaven CTO), Marcus O'Neill (Platform), Priya Desai (Security), Jamal Carter (DevOps), Nora Patel (Product)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone thanks for joining on time. this is Maya from Redwood, i'll hand over to diego shortly for the technical bit but first quick intro and goals for today.
[00:18] Emma Li: Hey thanks Maya, appreciate it. want to make sure this is practical — we need the platform in staging in ~3 weeks and a plan for production rollout by end of May. main concerns are observability and data residency.
[00:32] Diego Ramos: great, thanks. quick outline: runbook & access, networking (vpc/peering), security (kms, sso), observability in Redwood Console, perf targets and a short dedicated demo. sound right?
[00:47] Marcus O'Neill: yes. also cost predictability — if we go hosted vs dedicated how do we get consistent latency without ballooning cost.
[01:02] Lena Park: i'll cover how our batching and cache policies help cost + lat — and we can show ded/hosted tradeoffs.
[01:15] Priya Desai: quick note on compliance: we need SOC2 evidence, audit log retention, and key management options (HSM/KMS). also any data residency controls?
[01:28] Maya Chen: absolutely. we have a compliance pack, and Private (VPC/on-prem) options for residency. we can share docs — i'll add the security pack to next steps.
[01:42] Jamal Carter: network-wise we use strict egress rules, so we need peering details not just ip whitelist.
[01:49] Diego Ramos: understood. we'll request your vpc diagram and suggest a peering approach. for egress we can do NAT and controlled subnets, or dedicated placement.

[08:00] Diego Ramos: (technical) about observability — the Console exposes per-route and per-model latency breakdown, token cost estimate, and trace hooks. small caveat: autogen span names might show as "model-infer" in older builds — sorry the naming can be a bit funky in the UI.
[08:21] Marcus O'Neill: hmm naming weirdness is okay as long as we can map traces back to customer tokens and user IDs. do you support correlation ids?
[08:35] Diego Ramos: yes, we advise passing request_id and user_id; they show up in traces. there is also a token-level cost export CSV.

[15:02] Emma Li: timeline check — staging in three weeks is tight. who's owning the runbook tasks?
[15:12] Maya Chen: redwood will own the onboarding runbook delivery and initial console walkthrough. copperhaven to provision accounts/iam roles and provide network diagrams. we will pair for runner tests.

[22:40] Priya Desai: about keys — do you offer customer-managed keys (CMK) or only platform keys? we have to use our KMS for certain PII flows.
[22:52] Diego Ramos: we support KMS integration for Private and Dedicated. for hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer KMS via configuration — but for full HSM-level separation we recommend Private.
[23:09] Priya Desai: okay good. can you put that in writing with the exact artifact names?
[23:14] Maya Chen: yes, i'll include the KMS integration doc and a matrix of feature availability across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

[30:05] Marcus O'Neill: perf targets: we need 95th percentile latency <120ms for short responses up to 256 tokens; and sustained throughput ~200 requests/minute. can you validate those on the dedicated pool?
[30:21] Diego Ramos: that's a helpful baseline. we'll run a quick benchmark on a dedicated config and share the results. quick note: the latency depends on model variant and quantization; we usually recommend a quantized variant for cost savings with a small latency tradeoff.
[30:42] Lena Park: also auto-batching windows and cache hit rates matter; we'll share suggested batch sizing and KV cache warm-up steps.

[38:10] Nora Patel: product question — do you have built-in evals or quality monitoring tied to prompt sets? we want alerts on regressions.
[38:22] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts linked to prompt sets; we can enable a baseline eval during pilot.

[45:50] Emma Li: procurement note — what are typical contract lead times for Dedicated? our procurement needs SLAs and pricing bands.
[45:59] Maya Chen: Dedicated is usually a reserved capacity contract monthly or annual. i'll send a standard pricing sheet; if you need specific SLA language we'll loop in sales/legal.

[50:00] Jamal Carter: small concern — does the platform store raw transcripts? data retention and retention policy for logs is important.
[50:11] Diego Ramos: logs and transcripts retention is configurable; we can redact PII at ingestion and we have retention controls per-tenant. for legal export we provide audit log dumps.

[54:30] Maya Chen: ok recap and next steps: we'll send the runbook, security pack, and KMS matrix. diego will run the perf template and schedule a short dedicated demo next tuesday. customer to share vpc diagram and IAM contacts.
[54:50] Emma Li: sounds good. can we get those docs by Friday?
[54:55] Maya Chen: yes — i'll email them by EOD Friday (2026-04-08).
[55:05] Marcus O'Neill: thanks everyone, looking forward to the demo.
[55:10] Priya Desai: thanks.
[55:12] Meeting end.

Shared artifacts: onboarding_runbook_v2.pdf (drive link), perf-benchmark-template.xlsx (shared), security_compliance_pack_v1.zip (link).

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-heard product names (eg "RV cache" instead of KV cache), some background noise during Marcus's lines, speaker labels auto-generated and may shift for short segments.
